conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s simply a well-researched checklist that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, so we can offer the right support. Everything we discuss stays between you, me, and the clinical team unless you tell me there’s an immediate safety concern. We’ll go through ten questions about the past seven days; you can answer in your own words, and we’ll take it at your pace. Ready to begin?

First question: Overall, in the past week, how much have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly? Not very much. I used to laugh all the time—my husband and I would joke about everything—but lately even the things that used to crack me up just feel… flat. I might smile if something’s really silly, but it’s like the laughter gets stuck before it comes out.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not really... I mean, a couple of times I cracked a tiny smile when my husband made a goofy face at the baby, but it felt forced. Most of the week, even when I know something’s supposed to be funny, I just feel too heavy to laugh.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much at all. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but now it’s like I have to force myself to care. Once in a while I’ll think, “It might be nice to watch that show,” but when the time comes I mostly feel “what’s the point?” and stay on the couch.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby spits up more than usual, I immediately think it’s because I ate something wrong or didn’t burp him long enough. When he wouldn’t settle the other night, I kept replaying everything I’d done and telling myself I must be missing some “mom instinct” everyone else has. I know, rationally, babies just cry sometimes, but I still feel like it’s my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly think, “What if she chokes? What if I fall asleep and drop her?” I check the monitor a dozen times at night, sure something’s wrong even when she’s perfectly fine. I know it’s not rational, but the thoughts just keep looping and I can’t switch them off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A few times this week—like yesterday in the grocery store—I suddenly felt my heart racing and I couldn’t catch my breath. There wasn’t any real danger; I just kept thinking the baby was going to get sick from the cart or someone would bump into her. I had to stand in the freezer aisle doing that slow-breathing thing until the shaking stopped.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah, most days I feel like I’m drowning. There’s bottles to wash, laundry piling up, the baby won’t nap unless I’m holding her, and I’m running on maybe four broken hours of sleep. I keep thinking, “I can’t do this,” but I still get up and push through. It’s exhausting—like I’m barely treading water and waiting for the next wave to hit.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I have trouble falling asleep almost every night. My mind keeps racing with all the “what-ifs” about the baby, and once I do drift off I wake up again worrying that I didn’t hear her cry. It’s like the sadness and the anxious thoughts just loop until I’m staring at the ceiling, counting down how little time I have left before she’s up again.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most of the week, yeah. I wake up already feeling heavy, like there’s this gray cloud hanging over everything. Little tasks feel huge, and I keep tearing up for no clear reason. There are moments when the baby smiles and I feel a flicker of something better, but it fades fast and the sadness settles right back in.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

A couple of times—like two evenings ago when she wouldn’t latch and I just felt useless. I sat in the rocker with her screaming and tears started rolling without me even realizing. It wasn’t just the feeding; it felt like everything piling up until I couldn’t stop the crying.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

Yeah… once or twice this week the thought just popped in—like “what if I wasn’t here?” It scared me, because I don’t want to leave my baby, but it was more this fleeting, exhausted wish to escape everything. I don’t have a plan or anything, and I’d never act on it, but the idea did cross my mind.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 27: Screening Note – Postpartum Depression/Anxiety Screen

Patient-reported symptoms (past 7 days):
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, frequent tearfulness  
- Marked loss of interest/enjoyment in usual activities  
- Excessive self-blame and guilt regarding infant care  
- Daily, intrusive “what-if” worries; two episodes of panic (grocery, home)  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance problems tied to racing/anxious thoughts  
- Feeling “drowning”/overwhelmed by routine tasks; fatigue  
- Passive, non-specific suicidal ideation without plan or intent (“what if I wasn’t here”); patient denies desire to die and reports protective factors (baby, husband)

Pattern: Symptoms present most days, interfere with functioning, onset after delivery.  
Risk flags: Depressed mood + anhedonia + guilt + passive SI → elevated likelihood of major postpartum depressive episode; comorbid anxiety evident.

Screening conclusion: High clinical concern for postpartum depression with anxious features; safety risk identified (passive SI). Recommend immediate comprehensive assessment (PHQ-9/EPDS, safety plan) and referral for appropriate perinatal mental health services.
